requirements_stated: Monitor sucrose concentration in-line for a clear, colourless aqueous solution

Expected concentration range: 5 to 15 % w/w with a quality limit of plus or minus 0.3 % w/w
Analyzer located in a dry, safe room 10 m from the pipe
Measurement frequency: one reading every minute
Reference method: laboratory refractometer remaining in use

chemometrics_note: Partial least squares (PLS) calibration models must be constructed using spectra acquired across the 5 to 15 % w/w sucrose range, incorporating scatter correction and temperature compensation.
realtime_tracking_note: Continuous 1-minute interval spectral acquisitions can be logged and processed in real time to monitor sucrose concentration trends.
future_direction: Integration of automated temperature compensation or expansion to multi-component monitoring if additional solutes are introduced.

proposal.what_would_change_it: Incompatibility of probe seals with daily hot caustic cleaning or unacceptable light attenuation over the 10 m silica fiber link.
proposal.next_step: Perform benchtop multi-method trials using representative aqueous sucrose samples referenced against your laboratory refractometer.

brief_answer: For monitoring your clear aqueous sucrose solution, we recommend starting with NIR spectroscopy using a transmission or transflection probe connected via Vis-NIR silica fibers to the analyser 10 m away. A feasibility trial with representative 5 to 15 % w/w samples referenced against your laboratory refractometer will establish the chemometric calibration model. Material compatibility with daily hot caustic CIP remains to be confirmed.
